content: Moderate-intensity statin therapy, as defined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), aims to achieve a reduction in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels by approximately 30–49%. The specific medications and their respective dosages for this category of therapy include: Atorvastatin at a dosage of 10–20 mg daily. Rosuvastatin at a dosage of 5–10 mg daily. Simvastatin at a dosage of 20–40 mg daily. Pravastatin at a dosage of 40–80 mg daily. Lovastatin at a dosage of 40 mg daily. Fluvastatin XL (extended-release formulation) at a dosage of 80 mg daily. Pitavastatin at a dosage range of 1–4 mg daily.
